summary: No held single-name thesis is broken by evidence in the files. All nine held stocks (DPZ, CARG, IDXX, INCY, FAST, KR, MSCI, VRSN, WMT) are still on the 11-10 menu with F-scores of 7-9, CFO above net income and no flags. The only flags on the menu (amended 10-K/10-Q) sit on GRMN and ONC, neither held. Today's two fills (MSM sold at $121.45, INCY bought at $119.37) did not change that. The day was +0.56% for the agent against +1.32% for SPY since version 6 began, which says nothing about fundamentals. The MSM sale was a sleeve-consolidation and risk call, not a fundamental one: MSM was F9 with CFO $306.5M against net income $222.6M, stronger on paper than FAST (F8, CFO $1,295.9M against $1,258.4M), and the PM said so. No lesson in learning.json names the Fundamentals Analyst. L3 and L6 evidence cite this review, so I kept the label-artifact and stale-text checks below. There are no graded fundamentals calls to learn from yet.
update: Holdings check against fundamentals.json, by thesis clause. DPZ: the stored invalidation includes 'a fundamentals screen drops it from the menu or shows CFO below net income'. It is still on the menu (F8, CFO $792.1M against net income $601.7M, gp_sector_pct 1.0), so that clause is untripped. Its Consumer Staples rank is still a wholesale-groceries SIC artifact. FAST: the 'operating cash flow clearly below net income' clause is untripped, but the margin is the thinnest of the held names ($1,295.9M against $1,258.4M) and gross_margin_improved is false. Its menu label is Consumer Discretionary (SIC retail-building materials), while the new thesis text calls it Industrials by bucket. The bucket reading is the right one for the business. CARG (F8, gp 1.0, CFO $295.3M against $155.9M) and VRSN (F9, gp 0.993, CFO $1,091.1M against $825.7M) remain the best-supported holdings on the numbers. IDXX (F8, gp 0.942) and MSCI (F8, gp 0.904, leverage_not_up false, labelled Industrials, which is a SIC artifact for an index and analytics business) are unchanged. KR and WMT are both F7, the screen minimum, so one failed test would drop them off the menu. KR's latest fiscal year ended 2026-01-31, as did WMT's, and both data sets are about nine months old. INCY (new today): F8 with asset_turnover_improved false and CFO $1,413.5M against net income $1,286.7M. The PM's stored invalidation measures the $110 stop from the 11-10 close of $121.89 and says it will be restated from the actual $119.37 fill at the next run. Under L6 that restatement is due. Its SIC label ('commercial physical and biological research') is loose, but the Health Care sector is right. Data age, for every held name: the screen still uses FY2025 10-Ks for DPZ, CARG, IDXX, INCY, MSCI, VRSN and FAST, so it does not reflect the Q3 prints that came out in late October and early November. A thesis clause that leans on 'fundamentals' is therefore tested against data 10-11 months old. Holdings not on the menu: BND, IEF, VNQ, VOO and VTI are funds that the stock screen never covers, so their absence is not a fundamental signal. Their risk is in the price stops. BND and IEF closed 1.6% above their stops ('near'), a rates question for the Market Analyst, not an accounting one. MSM (sold): the sale's invalidation (MSM beats SPY and INCY by more than 3 points over 20 sessions) is pending. MSM stays a fundamentally clean candidate if the industrial sleeve is ever rebuilt. Process note for tomorrow: rank KR and WMT below the F8-F9 names when weighing adds, because they sit at the F7 floor.
